clue.text: Where flautist sits after late film

indicators.note: 'after' tells the solver that the orchestral position is written following the word for late

blocks.note: late in the sense of dead and departed
flutes are woodwind, so a flautist sits with the wind section of an orchestra

explanation.surface: An orchestra's seating plan, or a musician's mention of where they sat after a late screening.
explanation.walkthrough: The four-word title is built in two halves: a word for late, then the orchestral section a flute player belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone with the Wind is the 1939 Hollywood epic starring Vivien Leigh and Clark Gable.

clue.text: Mr Caine's perverted, says maid, one discovered in bed

indicators.note: something perverted is twisted out of its proper form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the actor Michael Caine
the fodder, eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A maid gossips that the film star has been corrupted and was caught in someone's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not a bedroom: the definition is a plant found growing there. The 's is just 'is' joining the actor to his fate.
explanation.definitionFit: A Michaelmas daisy is an autumn-flowering aster, a plant a gardener finds growing in a flower bed.

clue.text: Next ruler half-heartedly accepted by small group

indicators.note: doing something half-heartedly here means losing half of the word's heart, one of its two central letters
being accepted by a group means being taken inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a queen is a ruler
a subset is a smaller group within a set

explanation.surface: Who rules next is decided by a small committee that only half-heartedly accepts the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruler has a doubled letter at its heart, so half-heartedly removes just one of that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsequent means coming after in order or time, the same as next.

clue.text: Polish workers go up

blocks.note: worker bees are the classic crossword workers
to wax is to grow or increase, as the moon does

explanation.surface: Polish labourers move up in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb or noun for shining a surface; the capital is just the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Beeswax is used as a polish for furniture and floors, rubbed on to give a shine.

clue.text: Almost say no to stimulant

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: to spurn is to reject, to say no

explanation.surface: Someone nearly turns down a pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is an incentive or stimulus that drives someone on, as a rider's spur drives a horse.

clue.text: Garden wall covering exotic rare piece previously undisturbed

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so these letters take an unfamiliar new order
previously says the word for undisturbed comes earlier, standing before the rearranged letters

blocks.note: virgin territory or snow is untouched, undisturbed
the fodder, nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rare and exotic item was previously left untouched beneath the garden wall's cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia creeper is a climbing vine commonly grown to cover garden walls, famous for its red autumn leaves.

clue.text: London landmark overlooked by partially-sighted columnist

definitions.text: London landmark overlooked by partially-sighted columnist

blocks.clueFragment: London landmark overlooked by partially-sighted columnist
blocks.note: surface reading: a famous London spot watched over by a newspaper writer with poor eyesight
setter's reading: Admiral Nelson, who lost the sight of one eye, stands on top of his column overlooking the square

explanation.walkthrough: A columnist usually writes a newspaper column; here it is someone who stands on one. Nelson's Column dominates the square, and Nelson was blind in one eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The square in central London is overlooked by Nelson's Column, topped by a statue of the one-eyed admiral.

clue.text: Privacy I lost due to reform

indicators.note: to reform something is to give it a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: Someone laments losing their privacy because of a reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitude is the state of being alone and undisturbed, which is what privacy gives you.

clue.text: Peer touring South American city finds religious house

indicators.note: touring means going all round something, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: to peer is to look closely, to pry
Rio de Janeiro in Brazil

explanation.surface: A nobleman on a tour of Rio comes across a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' suggests a lord, but it is the verb to look closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A priory is a monastery or convent governed by a prior or prioress, a type of religious house.

clue.text: Traps ambassador in tricky situation

indicators.note: in places one element inside the other, here the envoy inside the predicament

blocks.note: His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
a mess is a tricky situation

explanation.surface: A diplomat is caught in an awkward predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: HE, for His Excellency, is the standard crossword ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Meshes as a verb means entangles or catches in a net, so it can stand for traps.

clue.text: Dismiss two games (very loud) after call for quiet

indicators.note: after says the games and the loudness are written following the request for silence

blocks.note: the sound you make to ask for silence
RU is rugby union and GO is the Japanese board game
fortissimo in music notation

explanation.surface: Two noisy matches are waved away after someone calls for hush.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) and GO (a board game) are the two games; FF is the musical mark fortissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrug off a criticism or problem is to brush it aside, treating it as unimportant.

clue.text: Floor covering just short of top-notch, going west

indicators.note: just short means stopping one letter before the end of the word
in an across answer, going west means reading from right to left

blocks.note: elite means the very best, top-notch

explanation.surface: A floor covering that isn't quite first-rate is going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiles are laid as a hard floor covering, in kitchens and bathrooms especially.

clue.text: Prison dust-up reported to Yard

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so what counts is the sound

blocks.note: quod is old British slang for prison
a wrangle is a noisy quarrel, a dust-up

explanation.surface: A brawl in jail is reported to Scotland Yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' looks like Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters, but it is the definition: an enclosed courtyard. Quod is dated British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrangle is a four-sided courtyard enclosed by buildings, as in a college, which is a kind of yard.

clue.text: Performing his parodies, I omitted to express emotion

indicators.note: omitted means left out, so that letter is removed from the fodder
performing suggests putting something on in a new form, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, eleven letters
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A comedian performing parodies forgets a line and gets emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: One I comes out of HIS PARODIES before the shuffle, leaving ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To rhapsodise is to speak or write with great enthusiasm, pouring out feeling.

clue.text: Cry from traveller turning back on impulse

indicators.note: turning back means facing the other way, so the word is read in reverse
on places the word for traveller after the word for impulse

blocks.note: a whim is a sudden impulse
a travelling sales representative

explanation.surface: A traveller cries out as they impulsively turn back.
explanation.walkthrough: A rep (sales representative) is the crossword's usual traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimper is a low, feeble cry, such as one of pain or fear.

clue.text: Festival chief sacks English knight

indicators.note: to sack is to dismiss, so the letter for English is thrown out

blocks.note: a gala is a festival or celebration
the head is the chief
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: The festival's boss fires an Englishman of noble rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad is the purest knight of King Arthur's Round Table, the one who found the Holy Grail.

clue.text: Item that's broadcast rising in volume

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means reading the word from bottom to top
in places the rising word inside the book word

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it by scattering
a tome is a large book, a volume

explanation.surface: A news item that has been broadcast is turned up louder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' and 'volume' both pretend to be about radio; broadcast here means scattering seed, and volume is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a couple in a relationship, and a twosome is a pair of people.

clue.text: Great gathering army has depopulated boroughs

indicators.note: gathering says the abbreviation collects the next word alongside it to form one unit

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for great
a host is an army or great multitude
boroughs are towns

explanation.surface: A huge massing of troops has emptied the towns.
explanation.walkthrough: The word boroughs serves twice, in the wordplay and as part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghost towns are settlements abandoned by their inhabitants, left empty and deserted.

clue.text: Old light dart

blocks.note: first meaning: a rushlight, a candle made from the pith of a ... dipped in fat
second meaning: to move quickly, to hurry

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a vintage lightweight dart; in fact it is two separate senses of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushes dipped in tallow were burned as cheap lamps in the past, and to dart is to move fast.

clue.text: Cornish fires not hot? You'll need these

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for hot is taken away

blocks.note: Cornwall is in the South West of England
electric fires are heaters
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: If your Cornish holiday cottage's fires don't heat up, pack something warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition only works in context: with the fires not hot, you will need warm clothing. Sweaters are jumpers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweaters are warm knitted tops, exactly what you need to wear when the heating doesn't work.

clue.text: Little boy taking time with cuddly toy

indicators.note: taking here means taking away, so the letter for time is removed

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a teddy bear

explanation.surface: A small boy spends time with his cuddly toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddy is a pet form of Edward, a name you would give a little boy.

clue.text: Round 1 fix due to terminate

indicators.note: to fix something can mean to rig or doctor it, so these letters are rearranged
round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the numeral

blocks.note: the fodder, five letters
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boxing bout's first round, fixed, is due to end early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round 1' reads as a boxing round, but round is the container signal and 1 is the letter I, which the rearranged letters wrap around.
explanation.definitionFit: To die out is to come to an end gradually, as a custom or species does, so to terminate.

clue.text: Peacemakers employed by Mint

blocks.note: the United Nations
employed means put to use

explanation.surface: UN peacekeepers are hired by the Royal Mint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like the place that makes coins, but it is the adjective for brand new.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in mint condition is pristine, as if never used.

clue.text: Doctor cut by single clip picked up incorrectly

indicators.note: being cut by something means having it driven into you, so the other pieces go inside

blocks.note: Doctor of Medicine
I is one, single
to shear is to clip, as with sheep

explanation.surface: A doctor is wounded by one snip of the scissors.
explanation.definitionFit: Misheard means picked up wrongly by ear, the way you might pick up a message incorrectly.
